text:
Clouds have been stubborn this morning, and they're in no hurry to leave. We're in the low 40s under a gray lid, with maybe a stray flurry or sprinkle before it fades out early this afternoon. Nothing that amounts to anything. The warm air is already arriving above us, but the clouds are stuck underneath it, so I'd bet on a mostly gray afternoon, with maybe a late peek of sun before it sets at 4:24. The high lands around 44, and the European model is a touch warmer.

Tonight clears out and turns frosty, down to around 31, so give yourself a minute for the windshield in the morning. Then things flip. Tuesday is mostly sunny and a good deal milder, with a high near 51, and the mid 50s look likely Wednesday through Friday. The next real chance for showers holds off until Sunday, and even that could come up light. For today, a jacket is all you need, and the afternoon is fine for a walk, so no umbrella.

week.blurb: Clouds hang around today with a high near 44, then skies clear tonight and it turns chilly, around 31 by morning.
Sunshine returns and it's a good bit milder, with a high near 51, though the models run a couple degrees either side.
Mostly sunny and mild again, with the high pushing 55, a good day for a lunchtime walk.
Another mostly sunny, mild afternoon near 54, and tonight only dips to around 39, so no frost worries.
Looks like more sunshine and a high around 56, the warmest day of the stretch, with a dry evening.
The weekend starts mostly sunny and mild, near 55, so Saturday looks like the day for outdoor chores or a ride.
Still sunny and near 55, a bit breezy in the afternoon, then clouds thicken and a sprinkle is possible after 1am.

  1. Dry and warm conditions become established by mid-week.
  2. After a period of dry warm weather, chances for showers increase towards the end of the weekend.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 821 AM EST Monday... Have issued a quick update to add isolated flurries/sprinkles to the forecast this morning. Area webcams indicate some light snow falling across the northern Greens, and note a few sites in the Adirondacks are reporting light mist. Any precipitation will be very light and should remain fairly localized; it will gradually taper off by early afternoon. No other changes were needed.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: A potent ridge and associated area of surface high pressure will become established this week, making it feel as if it were still mid-October. In a classic El Nino pattern, deep troughing and strong surface lows over the Pacific have caused continuous southwest to westerly flow out west, flooding the Great Plains and western Canada with warm Pacific air. This has caused temperature anomalies in the 20-30+ degree range. This airmass will begin to arrive today aloft, but clouds will likely remain stuck under the inversion, so it will likely take until Tuesday to warm up. Some undercast is likely today due to a shrinking and lowering moisture layer. Starting Tuesday, highs in the 50s will prevail though 60 will be possible in some of the warmest areas. There will be a strong, persistent subsidence inversion, and it will aided by the fact that significantly more surface heat will be lost at night than will be able to be replenished by the sun during the day. Radiational cooling will help lows drop into the 20s and 30s, around climatological normals.Temperatures at summit level should reach well into the 40s and freezing levels look to eclipse 10,000 ft by late in the week. KEY MESSAGE 2: Surface high pressure will be centered south of our region Thursday night into Friday, then drift northward across our area Saturday before sliding east. This will provide the northern New York and Vermont area with mainly dry weather and temperatures warmer than seasonal normals. On Sunday a low pressure system north of the Great Lakes will track northeastward, and our region will be under southerly flow ahead of the cold front. Sunday could be the warmest of the period, but will see increasing clouds and chances for showers on Sunday as well. We may have a cold front cross the area Sunday and bring some scattered rain showers. But there is also a possibility with two low pressure centers that the better energy associated with each low will pass to our north and to our south, leaving us in between without a lot of precipitation. Still much to work out before we get to the end of next weekend, but at this time this may be our best chance for showers through the period.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) -Happy Monday! We really begin to flip the script weather-wise this week. Our Monday starts mainly cloudy, and clouds will be stubborn to clear, but I do think we find some gradual clearing and sunshine into this afternoon. Clouds will linger and be the most stubborn in the Northeast Kingdom and Northern New Hampshire, but they too may find some sunshine by this evening just before sunset. High temperatures are generally in the upper 30s and low to mid 40s. We fall back into the 20s and lower 30s tonight as skies really start to clear. Tuesday will feature mostly sunny skies overhead. Temperatures start to warm up as most of us warm into the upper 40s and lower 50s into the afternoon. That is only the start. Wednesday may feature a bit more clouds from time to time, but temperatures reach the mid to upper 50s for most. Sunshine looks to stick around through Thursday and Friday. Thursday looks similar to Wednesday with most in the mid to upper 50s. By Friday, most of us are talking upper 50s to even near 60. Next weekend looks to feature a mixture of sunshine and clouds for Saturday with high temperatures in the low to mid 50s. There could be a few showers by Sunday, but at this point that chance is not looking all that impressive with temperatures again in the low to mid 50s.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-15T23:24:00Z — same caveat): Stubborn clouds and chill on Monday, a little late day sun — Clouds will be stubborn on Monday, though a few late-day breaks of sun are likely. Highs again reach the low 40s. Tuesday marks the transition toward brighter and warmer weather. Expect a mix of sun and clouds, with highs near 50. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with partly to mostly sunny skies and highs reaching the mid to upper 50s. The quiet pattern likely continues into the beginning of Thanksgiving week, although temperatures will fall closer to typical November highs in the 30s and 40s.
